steps.text: In a medium-size mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, milk, egg and salt.
Heat a large frying pan or wok over medium high heat. When the pan is hot add a teaspoon of butter and lightly coat the surface of the pan with the melted butter.
Pour one quarter cup of the batter into the pan and tilt the pan with a circular motion so that the batter coats the surface in a smooth and even layer.

After two minutes, lift up an edge of the crepe with a spatula to see if it is browning. When the underside has begun to brown, flip the crepe and cook the other side until it is also brown; about 2 minutes.
Repeat steps 3 and 4 to cook the remaining crepes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Breakfast Crepes
raw_recipe.description: The French surely have a way with these simple ingredients of egg, milk and flour. Swirl them together in a pan with melted butter for these delectable, ultra-thin pancakes that can be topped with powdered sugar. A Delicious simple recipe for the morning. You can double it to to make more.

review.reviewBody: Excellent! I haven't had crepes like this since I was little. I added an additional 1/4 cup of milk though which thinned the batter out and made it easier to make thin crepes. I read the other reviews and it sounds like they may just have their pan too hot. Start off low with just enough butter to coat the pan well. The gradually increase the heat and again decrease if it starts to turn the butter brown quickly. Reapet the bit of butter on each crepe that is cooked. This helps it get it's outer edge crispness without being dry. Yummy!

yummy! Last time I ate these was when my mom made them about 60 years ago. Yeah, a long time. They are so easy & tasty. Doubled the recipe to get enuf to share with hubby. Made a few with scrambled eggs, crumbeled bacon & cheese filling. He never had crepes before & now he's hooked.
I made these dairy free and grain free by using cassava flour and almond milk. Turned out great!

This is one of the better recipes I've tried for crepes. They have really nice crispy edges. I used butter flavored crisco instead of butter. I also added vanilla, a dash of sugar, and used a little half and half with 2% milk. Definitely keep the temp low and I reapplied crisco after every two crepes.

Although the flour and egg mixture looked like a hot mess, once I started adding the water/milk slurry it loosened up nicely and the butter just added a silky texture. Cooked up nicely, didn’t stick and were light as air.

turned out great. after reading the reviews I cooked on medium-low heat and I added a dash of sugar and vanilla extract to the batter. I used a medium pan (the desired size of crepe) with a small amount of butter added to coat the pan after each. crepe. They came out the perfect texture and flavor. I filled with strawberries and whip cream then sprinkled a sugar/cinnamon mixture to the outside. For me this recipe makes closer to 5 or 6 crepes.

This was an easy recipe. I put everything in a blender at night, gave it a whirl, used in the morning after a quick whirl again. Made pumpkin crepes by adding some cinnamon and ginger in the batter, topping with a scoop of pumpkin roll filling (Pumpkin Roll II), buttermilk syrup, and sprinklings of powdered sugar and cinnamon. The batter is thick and there are other recipes available that spread easier.

This was great, the batter seemed a bit thick so i added a bit more milk (not a ton) and served with fruit and whipped cream, I used a relatively small pan and they were very easy to flip. I decided to add butter between each crêpe so they wouldn’t stick to the pan, overall this is definitely a keeper.
Great recipe! Instead of whisking it I decided to use my blender, added a teaspoon of vanilla, and did about a cup and a half to 2cups of milk because the batter was too thick.

This recipe is not good. The proportion of milk and flour are the same and they can't be. They need to be closer to 4 to 1. The recipe needs to be 1 cup of milk and 1/4 flour so the batter is really thin making a paper thin crepe. The recipe the way it is came out like dough.
I added cinnamon and a little sugar to the batter and an additional 1/4 C of milk to make them thinner.
This is easy and delicious, I added dash of vanilla but the recipe is great just the way it is. Thank you
I added a little brown sugar to the mix
It was really good. But it took longer than I thought. Still pretty good and easy.
Too thick needs more liquid not thin enough
The crepes were so good. And the recipe was easy to follow.
My 7 year old grandson and I made these for breakfast today and they were delicious. We served them with cooked apples but he added some syrup too. Very easy and quick. I like better than pancakes

I used this recipe to make my first ever crepe. It is very simple which makes it easily modifiable. Though I did not make changes to the recipe, the results still varied because of variables like cooking duration and the amount of heat.
This recipe was amazing! will totally use again, recommended for everybody! (unless your gluten free like me)
